text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Medical oncology consultation to take over adjuvant endocrine therapy, confirm that no further adjuvant treatment is needed, and arrange germline genetic testing
  • Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for an initial five years, with venous thromboembolism symptoms, mood, hot flashes, sexual side effects, adherence, and interacting medicines reviewed at every visit
  • Genetic counseling and germline multigene panel testing (including BRCA2, BRCA1, PALB2, CHEK2, and ATM), with a letter for first-degree relatives explaining the result
  • Bone health: DXA at baseline, vitamin D repletion, dietary calcium, and weight-bearing exercise; bone-modifying drugs only for osteoporosis, not to prevent recurrence
  • Survivorship surveillance: cancer-related history and examination of both sides of the chest wall and both axillae every 3 to 6 months for 3 years, then every 6 to 12 months to 5 years, then yearly; no routine imaging, blood tests, or tumor markers without symptoms; lymphedema checks
  • Distress screening at each visit, at least 150 minutes of activity a week, and a written survivorship care plan

resource.title: Edward W. Brooke synthetic care plan
resource.description: Men get breast cancer. Care for a man of 83 with node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer after bilateral mastectomy, on the ASCO male breast cancer guideline and the NCCN breast guideline: tamoxifen as the preferred adjuvant endocrine therapy for men (not an aromatase inhibitor alone), with venous thromboembolism, mood, hot flash, sexual side effect, and adherence checks at every visit; germline genetic testing and genetic counseling offered to every man with breast cancer, with information for relatives; bone health on hormone therapy at his age; and survivorship care with no routine imaging or tumor markers. His own public account, that he dismissed his symptoms and had never had his chest examined, frames the teaching on why men present late.
